title: Three-Height Stationary Dribble
description: Players dribble in place at knee, waist and shoulder height on the coach's call, learning to control the bounce before they move.

content.objective: Control the ball at three dribble heights with either hand, using fingertips and a soft wrist, while keeping the eyes up.
content.setup: Each player has a ball and a personal spot spread across the court, facing the coach.
content.organization: Whole group at once. The coach calls 'low', 'middle' or 'high' and the hand to use.
instructions: Start in an athletic stance: feet shoulder-width, knees bent, chest up, eyes on the coach.
On 'low', dribble at knee height with quick, short bounces.
On 'middle', dribble at waist height: the normal control dribble.
On 'high', dribble at shoulder height as if pushing the ball in transition, without standing up straight.
Switch hands on the call and repeat all three heights.
coachingPoints: Push the ball down with the finger pads, not the palm.
The lower the dribble, the lower your hips: the ball and your body go down together.
Keep the off arm up as a shield.
Eyes on the coach, never on the ball.
commonMistakes: Slapping the ball with a flat palm.
Standing straight up for the high dribble and losing the stance.
Looking down at the ball between calls.
content.safety: Spread players out so dropped balls do not roll under others' feet; younger players use a size 5 or 6 ball.
progressions: Call heights faster and mix in 'switch' (change hands without stopping).
Add a second ball for advanced players.
regressions: Start with two-hand catches between dribbles for U8 players.
Allow players to glance at the ball for the first rounds.
variations: Partners face each other and call heights for each other.
Add a count: how many low dribbles in 20 seconds?
successCriteria: Ten controlled dribbles at each height with each hand without a lost ball.
Answers the coach's call within one dribble.
content.gameApplication: Low dribbles protect the ball under pressure, high dribbles move it quickly in the open court; changing height on demand is the base of every move.
content.repetitions: 3 rounds of 30 s per hand, 15 s rest
